body:
WHAT
Prompt Lab is a small local web console (tools/prompt-lab) for viewing and editing every prompt the engine sends to the model. It sometimes needs to compile the repo with the TypeScript compiler (tsc). It never spawns 'npx tsc'; instead it resolves the compiler's own script file (typescript/bin/tsc) once and runs it with the same node binary that is running the server, with no shell involved.

WHY
On Windows npx is npx.cmd, and execFile without a shell cannot start a .cmd file; it fails with ENOENT. That failure was silent: promote reported 'typecheck failed' with an empty body, and startup printed 'BUILD FAILED' with no cause while serving stale prompts.

WHERE
tools/prompt-lab/server.mjs — constant TSC (createRequire(REPO/package.json).resolve('typescript/bin/tsc')), function tscBuild(timeout) (run(process.execPath, [TSC, '-b'], {cwd: REPO, timeout})), ensureBuilt() and promote() which call it and fall back to err.message when stdout/stderr are empty.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. Every child-process invocation of the compiler in server.mjs uses process.execPath as the command and an absolute path ending in typescript/bin/tsc as args[0]; the strings 'npx' and 'shell: true' do not appear in any execFile call (assert by reading the source or by stubbing node:child_process.execFile and recording calls).
2. When typescript cannot be resolved (simulate by a fake createRequire whose resolve throws), TSC is undefined and tscBuild() throws synchronously with a message that mentions running npm install, rather than attempting a spawn.
3. With execFile stubbed to reject with an error that has empty stdout and stderr but a message 'spawn ENOENT', ensureBuilt() prints 'BUILD FAILED' followed by that message text (not a bare header), and promote() returns {ok:false, reverted:true} whose reason contains 'ENOENT'.
4. On a Windows host, calling tscBuild(60000) against the real repo resolves (or rejects with compiler output) instead of rejecting with ENOENT, proving no .cmd shim is in the path.
